channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Association Between Early Postoperative Limb Symmetry Index Scores and 2-Year Patient-Reported Outcomes After Quadriceps Tendon Autograft ACL Reconstruction.
item.description: A case series study of 100 patients after quadriceps tendon autograft ACL reconstruction found that early postoperative limb symmetry index (LSI) scores, particularly 3-month isometric quadriceps LSI, independently predicted 2-year patient-reported outcomes (IKDC and Lysholm scores). Patients achieving IKDC PASS generally attained a 60% to 70% LSI score by 3 months.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Post burn Cubital Tunnel Syndrome Electrophysiological and Functional Responses to High intensity Laser Therapy versus Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (N=75) on post-burn cubital tunnel syndrome found that both high-intensity laser therapy (HILT) and extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) combined with ulnar nerve gliding exercises improved nerve conduction and upper-limb function more than UNGE alone. HILT demonstrated superior electrophysiological (ulnar motor nerve conduction velocity, CMAP amplitudes) and functional (DASH scores) outcomes compared to ESWT, with benefits maintained at 12-week follow-up.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Reframing hands-on musculoskeletal assessment as a measurement instrument rather than a technique debate: a theoretical framework applying COSMIN to HODA-A.
item.description: This theoretical paper proposes Hands-On Data Acquisition and Analysis (HODA-A) as a framework for conceptualizing hands-on musculoskeletal examination as a clinician-reported outcome measurement process, rather than isolated manual techniques.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The effect of functional inspiratory muscle training on diaphragm function and core stabilisation in patients with chronic non-specific low back pain: a randomised controlled trial
item.description: A 10-week multicomponent functional inspiratory muscle training (F-IMT) program significantly improved diaphragm thickness (adjusted difference, 2.434 mm; 95% CI, 1.714 to 3.261; P < .001) and mobility, pain, respiratory muscle strength, and core stabilization in 40 CNSLBP patients compared to thoracic expansion exercises.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Credibility and strength of evidence for exercise, nutritional, and combined interventions on muscle function and physical performance in older adults: an umbrella review of meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials
item.description: An umbrella review of 28 meta-analyses of RCTs found the most consistently supported evidence for exercise-based interventions, particularly for fall-related outcomes, in older adults. Nutrition-only interventions showed modest benefits for muscle mass in vulnerable populations, and combined interventions improved some strength and functional outcomes.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Effects of thoracic kinesiological taping on pulmonary functions, respiratory muscle strength, and functional independence in patients with hemiplegia: a randomized controlled clinical trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=30) found that thoracic kinesiology taping combined with conventional rehabilitation significantly improved pulmonary function (FVC p<0.001, FEV1 p<0.001, PEF p<0.001) and maximal inspiratory pressure (p<0.001) in chronic post-stroke hemiplegia patients.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of kinesio taping and myofascial release therapy in cervicogenic headache: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=81) found both kinesio taping (KT) and myofascial release (MFR) combined with home exercise significantly reduced pain and headache frequency in cervicogenic headache patients, with MFR showing more sustained improvements in disability and physical quality of life.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of treadmill exercise with and without vertical traction on gait, pain, disability, trunk proprioception, and depression in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain: A randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=45) found that adding vertical traction and partial body weight support to treadmill exercise (VT+TE) significantly improved TUG performance, self-selected gait speed, disability, and flexion/extension repositioning errors more than treadmill exercise alone (TE) or core stabilization in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain. Both VT+TE and TE improved pain and depressive symptoms.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes and Factors Associated With Response in Older Adults With Massive Irreparable Rotator Cuff Tears: A Four-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
item.description: A 4-year prospective cohort study of 92 older adults with atraumatic massive irreparable rotator cuff tears found that 76 patients showed clinically important improvements with nonoperative treatment (physical therapy, home exercises, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injection) that persisted for 4 years. Smoking and longer symptom duration were associated with worse shoulder function.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of Sensory Electrical Stimulation Versus Alternating Electromyography-Guided Electrical Stimulation on Functional Recovery of the Hand in Chronic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A three-arm randomized controlled trial (n=60) in chronic stroke patients found that both sensory electrical stimulation (SES) and alternating electromyography-guided electrical stimulation (Alt-EMG), combined with conventional physical therapy, significantly improved upper-limb motor function (adjusted mean gains of 12.05 and 12.44 points on ARAT, respectively, versus control, both P < .001) over 12 weeks, with no significant difference between SES and Alt-EMG.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Can Psychological Readiness Predict Successful Return to Sports After Patellar Stabilization Surgery in Adolescent Patients? A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: A retrospective cohort study of 97 adolescent patients found that an ACL-RSI score ≥59.2 was significantly associated with successful return to sport (78.3% achieved RTS) after patellar stabilization surgery, with an odds ratio of 3.56 (95% CI, 1.10-11.51; P = .033).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Six-month supervised telerehabilitation combining pilates-based therapeutic exercise and self-myofascial release in adults with fibromyalgia: a randomized controlled trial | Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine
item.description: A 6-month supervised telerehabilitation program combining Pilates-based therapeutic exercise and self-myofascial release significantly improved fibromyalgia impact (partial η²=0.132), sleep quality (partial η²=0.129), depressive symptoms (partial η²=0.129), and perceived stress (partial η²=0.065) in 68 adults with fibromyalgia.
item.author: J Rehabil Med

item.title: Digital therapeutic combining exercise and cognitive-behavioural therapy reduces pain in patients with chronic patellofemoral pain: a multicentre randomised controlled trial
item.description: A multicenter RCT found a smartphone-based digital therapeutic combining personalized exercise and CBT significantly improved pain, function, quality of life, and psychological well-being in patients with chronic patellofemoral pain.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Effectiveness of conservative interventions on pain and disability in degenerative cervical spine disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 RCTs (2,378 participants) on degenerative cervical spine disease found that conservative interventions significantly reduced pain (SMD = −0.67, 95% CI: −0.97 to −0.37) and disability (SMD = −0.60, 95% CI: −0.97 to −0.24). Acupuncture and exercise-based interventions showed significant benefits, while manual therapy did not demonstrate a significant pooled benefit. The certainty of evidence was low.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Effects of Exercise Training on the Metabolic Cost of Walking in Health and Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 27 studies (1,177 participants) found that chronic physical exercise training improved the metabolic cost of walking (Cw) (g = 0.40, p = 0.001) across healthy adults and individuals with neurological conditions. Improvements were significant in healthy individuals (g = 0.49, p = 0.001) but smaller in stroke patients (g = 0.24, p = 0.065). Population moderated the effects of training on Cw (p = 0.043), with higher BMI associated with smaller effects.
item.author: Sports Medicine

item.title: Modality-specific, deficit-targeted exercise prescriptions for physical function in sarcopenia and frailty: a network meta-analysis
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 61 RCTs (3,706 participants) on sarcopenia and frailty found that multicomponent training with resistance training offered the most comprehensive benefits for functional mobility (low certainty). Elastic band resistance training was most effective for handgrip strength (MD 1.95 kg; 95% CI, 1.13 to 2.76; moderate certainty), and machine-based resistance training showed intermediate effectiveness for knee extension strength (MD 2.96 kg; 95% CI, 1.59 to 4.34; low certainty).
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Adherence to home-based exercise therapy in adults with non-specific chronic low back pain: a cross-sectional study of 491 participants of the ComPaRE cLBP e-cohort (ADHERE II).
item.description: A cross-sectional study of 491 adults with non-specific chronic low back pain found that 45% adhered to home-based exercise therapy. Higher pre-cLBP physical activity, lower pain intensity, and lower treatment burden were associated with better adherence, but supervision did not significantly influence it.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Continuity of care interventions for people with stroke and their caregivers: a scoping review of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: A scoping review of 65 randomized controlled trials on continuity of care interventions for stroke patients and caregivers found that most interventions focused on transitions from acute inpatient to home care, often excluding caregivers. It emphasizes the need for family-centered approaches across the entire care continuum.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: "It's not for me": community-based fall prevention exercise programs for those aging into disability.
item.description: A qualitative study with 11 adults aged 50+ with mobility/sensory impairments revealed multidimensional barriers to community-based fall prevention exercise programs, including physical, sensory, logistical, financial factors, and stigma. Participants often felt these programs were not for them due to a perception of weakness, highlighting a need for inclusive, flexible, and identity-affirming program co-design.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Technical and clinical feasibility of a pulmonary telerehabilitation model for people with COPD.
item.description: A two-phase feasibility study of a pulmonary telerehabilitation (PR) model for COPD found high technical feasibility (≥99% clinical agreement in data transmission) and clinical feasibility (19 participants completed the program, with high satisfaction/usability). Exploratory outcomes showed increased endurance time, suggesting the model is well-accepted but requires future RCTs for efficacy assessment.
item.author: PubMed
